subproblems.title: Velocities of curves in the image of a C¹ map with a continuous affine left inverse lie in the range of its derivative
subproblems.statement: Let d, P ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P, let L : ℝ^P → ℝ^d be a continuous linear map, and let z ∈ ℝ^P and s ∈ ℝ. Let D := B_s(0) ⊆ ℝ^d be the open ball. Assume Φ is of class C¹ on D and L(Φ(v) − z) = v for every v ∈ D. Put Σ := Φ(D). Then for every v₀ ∈ D, the contract's tangent space tangentSpace Σ (Φ(v₀)) is contained in the range of DΦ(v₀) = fderiv ℝ Φ v₀, regarded as a linear map and coerced to a set. That is, every w ∈ tangentSpace Σ (Φ(v₀)) equals DΦ(v₀)(y) for some y ∈ ℝ^d. Here tangentSpace Σ (Φ(v₀)) is the set of vectors w such that some γ : ℝ → ℝ^P is C¹ on (−1, 1), maps (−1, 1) into Σ, has γ(0) = Φ(v₀), and has HasDerivAt γ w 0. ℝ^m denotes Euclid m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (d P : ℕ) (Φ : Euclid d → Euclid P) (L : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid d) (z : Euclid P) (s : ℝ), ContDiffOn ℝ 1 Φ (ball 0 s) → (∀ v ∈ ball (0 : Euclid d) s, L (Φ v - z) = v) → ∀ v ∈ ball (0 : Euclid d) s, tangentSpace (Φ '' ball (0 : Euclid d) s) (Φ v) ⊆ (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ v : Euclid d →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P) : Set (Euclid P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0–4 of the supplied proof of the selected node dgce_left_inverse_tangentSpace_eq_range, unchanged in substance. This is the only part of that proof that uses the affine left inverse Pr(x) := L(x − z). Simon Ch. 2, §4, (4.3) (book/chapter-02.txt lines 865–871) states the tangent-space description without proof ('One readily checks').
Notation: ℝ^m := Euclid m. D := B_s(0) ⊆ ℝ^d (open ball). Σ := Φ(D). DΦ(v) := fderiv ℝ Φ v. Fix v₀ ∈ D and let T := tangentSpace Σ (Φ(v₀)). That is, T is the set of w ∈ ℝ^P for which some γ : ℝ → ℝ^P is C¹ on (−1, 1), maps (−1, 1) into Σ, has γ(0) = Φ(v₀), and has HasDerivAt γ w 0. The range of DΦ(v₀) means the set ↑(LinearMap.range ↑(DΦ(v₀))). A vector w lies in it iff w = DΦ(v₀)(y) for some y ∈ ℝ^d (LinearMap.mem_range), because the linear map underlying DΦ(v₀) evaluates as DΦ(v₀) itself (ContinuousLinearMap.coe_coe).
0. Setup. D is open (isOpen_ball) and v₀ ∈ D, so D ∈ 𝓝 v₀ (IsOpen.mem_nhds). Φ is C¹ on D, hence differentiable on D (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn_one), hence differentiable at v₀ (DifferentiableOn.differentiableAt). So Φ has Fréchet derivative DΦ(v₀) at v₀ (DifferentiableAt.hasFDerivAt).
1. Let w ∈ T with witness γ. So γ maps (−1, 1) into Σ, γ(0) = Φ(v₀), and HasDerivAt γ w 0. This inclusion does not use the C¹ property of γ. Put c(t) := L(γ(t) − z).
 - The map t ↦ γ(t) − z has derivative w at 0 (HasDerivAt.sub_const).
 - The continuous linear map L is its own Fréchet derivative at every point (ContinuousLinearMap.hasFDerivAt). By the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt), c has derivative L(w) at 0.
 - c(0) = L(γ(0) − z) = L(Φ(v₀) − z) = v₀, by the left-inverse hypothesis at v₀ ∈ D.
2. By step 0 and c(0) = v₀, Φ has derivative DΦ(v₀) at c(0). The chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt) then gives that Φ ∘ c, i.e. t ↦ Φ(L(γ(t) − z)), has derivative DΦ(v₀)(L(w)) at 0.
3. Let t ∈ (−1, 1). Then γ(t) ∈ Σ = Φ(D), so γ(t) = Φ(v) for some v ∈ D. By the left-inverse hypothesis at v, c(t) = L(Φ(v) − z) = v, so Φ(c(t)) = Φ(v) = γ(t). Since −1 < 0 < 1, the interval (−1, 1) is a neighbourhood of 0 (Ioo_mem_nhds). Hence γ = Φ ∘ c on a neighbourhood of 0, i.e. γ =ᶠ[𝓝 0] Φ ∘ c (filter_upwards).
4. By step 2 and this eventual equality, γ has derivative DΦ(v₀)(L(w)) at 0 (HasDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq). But γ also has derivative w at 0, so uniqueness of derivatives (HasDerivAt.unique) gives w = DΦ(v₀)(L(w)). Hence w lies in the range of DΦ(v₀), with witness y := L(w).
5. Since w ∈ T was arbitrary, T ⊆ range DΦ(v₀) as sets, i.e. tangentSpace (Φ '' ball 0 s) (Φ v₀) ⊆ ↑(LinearMap.range ↑(fderiv ℝ Φ v₀)). This holds for every v₀ ∈ D. ∎
proof_key_steps: Φ is differentiable at v₀ ∈ D because it is C¹ on the open ball.
For a witness γ of w, the curve c(t) := L(γ(t) − z) has c(0) = L(Φ(v₀) − z) = v₀ and, by the chain rule with the continuous linear map L, c'(0) = L w.
By the chain rule, Φ∘c has derivative DΦ(v₀)(L w) at 0.
For t ∈ (−1, 1), γ(t) = Φ(v) with v ∈ D, so c(t) = v and Φ(c(t)) = γ(t). Hence γ = Φ∘c on the neighbourhood (−1, 1) of 0.
So γ has derivative DΦ(v₀)(L w) at 0. Uniqueness of derivatives gives w = DΦ(v₀)(L w), so w ∈ range DΦ(v₀) with witness L w.

subproblems.title: Every vector Dψ(v)a is the velocity of a C¹ curve in N
subproblems.statement: Let P, r, d ∈ ℕ with r ≥ 1, N ⊆ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^d open, and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P of class C^r on V with ψ(V) ⊆ N. Then for every v ∈ V, Dψ(v)(ℝ^d) ⊆ tangentSpace N (ψ(v)), where Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v. Here tangentSpace N y is the set of w ∈ ℝ^P for which some γ : ℝ → ℝ^P is C¹ on (−1, 1), maps (−1, 1) into N, and satisfies γ(0) = y and γ'(0) = w (HasDerivAt γ w 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P r d : ℕ) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P), 1 ≤ r → IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ r ψ V → ψ '' V ⊆ N → ∀ v ∈ V, Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v) ⊆ tangentSpace N (ψ v)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0 and 5–8 of the supplied proof of the selected node dgce_left_inverse_tangentSpace_eq_range: the constant curve when a = 0, and the bounded sine reparametrization with the chain rule when a ≠ 0. Here they are restated for an arbitrary open V ⊆ ℝ^d, any target set N ⊇ ψ(V) and any smoothness order r ≥ 1. This is the exact frozen type of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dsmc_chart_range_subset_tangentSpace (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.mean_curvature_monotonicity-a1.chart_tangent_space-a1.range_subset_tangent-a1, candidate 8f402cb9), reused here unchanged.
The only change from the supplied argument is that the ball B_s(0) around the origin is replaced by a ball B(v, ρ₀) ⊆ V centred at the base point. The curve then stays within distance ρ₀/2 of v, instead of having norm at most ‖v₀‖ + (s − ‖v₀‖)/2.
Simon Ch. 2, §4, (4.3) (book/chapter-02.txt lines 865–871) states this inclusion without proof ('One readily checks'). The accepted Lean candidate uses the equivalent bounded reparametrization t/(1 + t²/c²) in place of the sine. The argument uses only that the reparametrization is C¹ and bounded, vanishes at 0 and has derivative 1 there.
Notation: ℝ^m := Euclid m. Dψ(v) := fderiv ℝ ψ v. tangentSpace N y is the set of w ∈ ℝ^P for which some γ : ℝ → ℝ^P is C¹ on (−1, 1), maps (−1, 1) into N, has γ(0) = y and HasDerivAt γ w 0.
0. Setup. Let P, r, d, N, V, ψ satisfy the hypotheses: 1 ≤ r, V is open, ψ is C^r on V, and ψ(V) ⊆ N. Fix v ∈ V.
 - Since 1 ≤ r in ℕ, also (1 : WithTop ℕ∞) ≤ (r : WithTop ℕ∞) (exact_mod_cast). So ψ is C¹ on V (ContDiffOn.of_le).
 - V is open and v ∈ V, so V ∈ 𝓝 v (IsOpen.mem_nhds). Hence ψ is differentiable at v (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn_one, then DifferentiableOn.differentiableAt), and ψ has Fréchet derivative Dψ(v) at v (DifferentiableAt.hasFDerivAt).
 - Let w ∈ Set.range Dψ(v), say w = Dψ(v)a with a ∈ ℝ^d. We construct a curve γ witnessing w ∈ tangentSpace N (ψ(v)).
1. Case a = 0. Then w = Dψ(v)0 = 0. Take the constant curve γ(t) := ψ(v).
 - γ is C¹ on (−1, 1) (contDiffOn_const).
 - For every t, γ(t) = ψ(v) ∈ ψ(V) ⊆ N, because v ∈ V (mem_image_of_mem).
 - γ(0) = ψ(v), and γ has derivative 0 = w at 0 (hasDerivAt_const).
 So w ∈ tangentSpace N (ψ(v)).
2. Case a ≠ 0: a bounded reparametrization. Then ‖a‖ > 0 (norm_pos_iff). Since V is open and v ∈ V, there is ρ₀ > 0 with ball(v, ρ₀) ⊆ V (Metric.isOpen_iff). Put c₀ := ρ₀/(2‖a‖) > 0 and θ(t) := c₀·sin(t/c₀). Then:
 - θ is C^∞, in particular C¹, on ℝ: Real.contDiff_sin composed with the linear map t ↦ t/c₀, times the constant c₀.
 - For every t, |θ(t)| = c₀·|sin(t/c₀)| ≤ c₀ (Real.abs_sin_le_one, c₀ > 0).
 - θ(0) = c₀·sin 0 = 0.
 - θ has derivative 1 at 0. The map t ↦ t/c₀ has derivative 1/c₀ at 0 (HasDerivAt.div_const). So t ↦ sin(t/c₀) has derivative cos(0)·(1/c₀) = 1/c₀ at 0 (HasDerivAt.sin, Real.cos_zero). Hence θ has derivative c₀·(1/c₀) = 1 at 0 (HasDerivAt.const_mul, c₀ ≠ 0).
3. Let κ(t) := v + θ(t)·a. Then:
 - κ is C¹ on ℝ: a constant plus the C¹ scalar function θ times the constant vector a (ContDiff.add, ContDiff.smul).
 - κ(0) = v + 0·a = v.
 - κ has derivative 1·a = a at 0 (HasDerivAt.smul_const, HasDerivAt.const_add, one_smul).
 - For every t ∈ ℝ, ‖κ(t) − v‖ = ‖θ(t)·a‖ = |θ(t)|·‖a‖ ≤ c₀‖a‖ = ρ₀/2 < ρ₀ (norm_smul). So κ(t) ∈ ball(v, ρ₀) ⊆ V.
4. Let γ := ψ ∘ κ. Then:
 - γ is C¹ on (−1, 1). Indeed, κ is C¹ on (−1, 1) and maps it, indeed all of ℝ, into V, where ψ is C¹ by step 0 (ContDiffOn.comp with ContDiff.contDiffOn and the MapsTo fact of step 3).
 - For t ∈ (−1, 1), κ(t) ∈ V, so γ(t) = ψ(κ(t)) ∈ ψ(V) ⊆ N.
 - γ(0) = ψ(κ(0)) = ψ(v).
 - ψ has derivative Dψ(v) at κ(0) = v (step 0), and κ has derivative a at 0 (step 3). By the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt), γ has derivative Dψ(v)a = w at 0.
 So γ witnesses w ∈ tangentSpace N (ψ(v)).
5. Steps 1–4 cover every w ∈ Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v). Hence Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v) ⊆ tangentSpace N (ψ v), and since v ∈ V was arbitrary, this holds for every v ∈ V. ∎
proof_key_steps: From 1 ≤ r and V open, ψ is C¹ on V and has Fréchet derivative Dψ(v) at each v ∈ V.
For a = 0, the constant curve at ψ(v) lies in ψ(V) ⊆ N and has velocity 0 = Dψ(v)0.

For a ≠ 0, choose ball(v, ρ₀) ⊆ V and c₀ = ρ₀/(2‖a‖). Then θ(t) = c₀ sin(t/c₀) is smooth with θ(0) = 0, θ'(0) = 1 and |θ| ≤ c₀, so κ(t) = v + θ(t)a stays in ball(v, ρ₀) ⊆ V, with κ(0) = v and κ'(0) = a.
γ = ψ∘κ is C¹ on (−1, 1), maps into ψ(V) ⊆ N and has γ(0) = ψ(v). By the chain rule, γ'(0) = Dψ(v)a, so range Dψ(v) ⊆ tangentSpace N (ψ v).
